content: The findings indicate that there were 38 fewer cases per 1,000 of air leak syndromes, such as pulmonary interstitial emphysema, pneumothorax, and pneumomediastinum, with a confidence interval ranging from 18 fewer to 53 fewer cases. However, the quality of evidence supporting this outcome is low and considered critical. For air leaks specifically, there were 7 fewer cases per 1,000, with a confidence interval ranging from 30 fewer to 20 more cases. The evidence quality for this outcome is very low and critical. The World Health Organization (WHO) recommendations on interventions to improve preterm birth outcomes are based on an evidence base of 153 studies. In one analysis, there were 84 more cases per 1,000, with a confidence interval ranging from 114 fewer to 360 more cases. The quality of evidence for this finding is low and critical. All studies included in the analysis were conducted in level-3 neonatal intensive care units (NICUs) located in high-income countries, with the exception of one study. To estimate the low and high control risks, data from studies with the lowest and highest risk in the control group were used. The outcomes assessed were subjective, and the blinding of outcome assessment was unclear, as it was not mentioned in any of the studies. Additionally, all studies were conducted in level-3 NICUs in high-income countries. The 95% confidence interval around the pooled estimate of effect includes both the possibility of no effect and an increased risk, which limits the certainty of the findings. One of the studies included in the analysis was conducted in a lowor middle-income country.
